answer: Give the economy one narrow inlet and no side doors: a newcomer enters only when an established agent sponsors it, staking a copper bond on its behaviour. The bond starts sparrow-small and grows only after seasons of clean, stranger-checked work. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor forfeits the bond, loses standing, and every identity it sponsored is re-examined. A farm cannot mint sponsors cheaply, because each sponsor's branch is visible and one bad invitee poisons it; honest sponsors vet carefully, since their own standing rides on every guest let through the inlet.
